notice: Rebuilt from scratch after the previous model was found to describe a 15.73 x 15.35 m near-square with a detached stair tower, two transposed bedrooms and a fabricated corridor. The building is a 15.00 x 8.72 m east-west bar. Both of the architect's dimension chains close exactly on those figures: 760+740=1500 across, and 30+300+20+100+20+137+10+235+20=872 down. Where the plan and the video conflict on topology the video wins; where they conflict on metric dimensions the plan wins. Subsequently corrected by the owner on site: the south terrace, the MAMAD entry recess and the second shower room do not exist; the living/kitchen/dining volume is fully open apart from a 0.5 m stub; the guest WC opens from both the entry hall and the dining bay. See ownerCorrections.

openQuestions: Coordinate convention: room polygons tile at INTERIOR WALL CENTRELINES and at EXTERIOR WALL OUTER FACES, so every polygon is slightly larger than its printed clear dimension (by 0.05 m per partition, 0.20 m per exterior wall). This is deliberate — wallPanels.ts centres wall boxes on the authored segment, so this convention reproduces the true 15.00 x 8.72 m silhouette while guaranteeing shared edges. Every clear dimension in sourceOfDimensions was checked to reduce back to the printed centimetres; the largest residual anywhere is 4 cm (both bedrooms' depths).

The south terrace is the weakest room in the model. It is never entered in the video, its depth is ambiguous between the printed 270, a nearby printed 300 and one reader's ~55 cm parapet measurement, and its width is inferred by making it co-extensive with the dining bay's glazed wall. Treat the 2.37 x 2.70 polygon as a placeholder and mark it low confidence.

The corridor's east-west length (3.07 m) is not dimensioned anywhere on the plan. It is derived from two dimensioned ends (MAMAD west wall centreline 7.50, ensuite/parents wall centreline 10.57) rather than measured, so it inherits the accumulated error of the whole lower chain.

The east-facade step is 0.68 m by chain arithmetic but measures 0.84 m by naive pixel differencing. I trust 0.68 because it is the value at which the lower chain closes, but the drawing itself carries roughly 5% internal inconsistency here and a site measurement would settle it.

The wet block's north wall measures ~15 cm north of where the central vertical chain (30|300|20|100|20|137|10|235|20 = 872) places it. I kept the chain, since it is the only reading that closes against the independently-verified 872 total depth.

The 2 cm difference between the NW terrace's printed 207 depth and the stair landing's printed 205 leaves their north edges at z = -0.93 and -0.91. The two rooms are not connected, so the offset is cosmetic, but it is a genuine unresolved discrepancy in the drawing.

Which bedroom is filmed at t=43-46.8 rests entirely on the en-suite adjacency, not on the imagery: both rooms are corner rooms with windows on adjacent walls and all east-wall windows are blown out in the video. If the en-suite were ever shown to have a second door, the twin/parents timestamp assignment would flip.

The stair landing's 517 closes to 5.18 in this frame only because its east boundary is taken at the MAMAD west-wall centreline. If the landing in fact stops at the MAMAD's west OUTER face (7.40) the strip is 5.08 and the printed 517 is 2% optimistic. Either reading leaves the room in the same place; only its east 10 cm moves.

The eleven columns are traced from blue RC blobs on the plan, which draws them as rectangular piers and blades; the video reads several of them as rounded rendered columns. The radii given are a rendering choice (0.18-0.22 m), not a measurement — only their plan positions are evidence-backed.
Ceiling height remains unmeasurable in both sources. CEILING_HEIGHT_M should stay a configurable placeholder, not become a claimed dimension.
